voice: Kāṇha, a kāpālika yogi, sings straight at Ḍombī, the Ḍom woman whose hut is outside the town: he teases and courts her, shows off his outcaste gear, then turns without warning to a flat threat. Plain, blunt, spoken-sung English, with hard calls ('Hey', 'You there') and short, heavily beaten lines.
refrainCue: Hey Ḍombī, I'll take up with

lines.en: touching, touching, goes that [brahmin]{brahmin} with shaven head.
Hey Ḍombī, I'll take up with you;
Hey [Ḍombī]{dombi}, in good faith I ask you:
you come, you go, [Ḍombī]{dombi}, in whose [boat]{boat}?
for you I've left the performer's basket.
For you I've put on a [garland of bones]{bone-garland}.

couplets.kept: Keeps the verbless first half, as in the source, and the doubled 'touching, touching' (chaichoi). The halves end on 'hut' and 'head', a consonant echo standing in for the full rhyme kuṛiā/nāṛiā; nāṛiā is sung as 'shaven head'.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme is only echoed. 'By' after 'goes' is dropped, and 1b runs three syllables longer than 1a.

couplets.kept: Keeps the call 'Hey', Kāṇha's self-naming and the source order of 2b, disgust first and 'clings' last, with k-sounds struck through it. 'Take up with' carries sāṅga's company and its erotic edge; 'unsqueamish' sings nirghṛṇa, approved 'without disgust'.
couplets.letGo: The near rhyme sāṅga/lāga is not matched: the halves end on 'you' and 'clings'. 'Take up with' begins a bond where 'keep company' holds one, and 2b is four syllables longer than 2a.

couplets.kept: Keeps the one lotus, its sixty-four petals and poor Ḍombī climbing and dancing, as two eight-syllable halves that both end on a falling two-syllable word (petals, dances), as the source ends on pākhuṛī and bāpuṛī.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme pākhuṛī/bāpuṛī: 'four' and 'poor' would rhyme only by twisting the word order. 'On it' (tahim̐) is compressed into 'up'.

couplets.kept: Keeps the calls to Ḍombī and the source order of 4b (you come, you go, Ḍombī, whose boat), ending on 'boat' like nābem̐. 'I ask you: / you come' links the halves; sadabhāve stays 'in good faith'.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme sadabhābe/nābem̐ is not matched; no honest English rhyme for 'boat' was found.

couplets.kept: Keeps cord, Ḍombī selling, 'no more baskets' (still open between 'no longer' and 'no other') and the performer's basket. Both halves end on 'basket', and 'for you I've' begins the anaphora 6b repeats, as tohora antare does.
couplets.letGo: The source's near rhyme joins two different words (caṅgatā, eṭṭā); here one English word repeats. 'Given up' is sung as 'left', and 'for your sake' as 'for you'.

couplets.kept: Keeps the call 'You there' (tu lo), the blunt self-declaration and the garland of bones; 'For you I've…' repeats the opening of 5b, as tohora antare repeats in the source.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme kapālī/mālī is lost: 'kāpālika' and 'bones' do not chime, and no honest rhyme was found. 'For your sake' is sung as 'for you'.

couplets.kept: Keeps lake, lotus root and the threat. Both halves are built alike, a subject and two verbs, with a chime running breaks, lake, take; the song ends flat on 'life', as the source ends on parāṇa.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme molāṇa/parāṇa is lost. 'Breaking' becomes 'breaks', and 7b drops the second 'I'll', so mārami and lemi share one subject.

questions: Refrain (2a): 'take up with' is chosen for sāṅga karibe because it keeps the social sting of a man taking up with an outcaste woman and the erotic sense; but it is inceptive and a little disreputable in tone. If you prefer the accurate English's sense unchanged, the fallback is 'Hey Ḍombī, you and I will keep company' (toe sama, 'together with you'), and the refrain cue would change with it.

Refrain (2b): 'unsqueamish' replaces the approved 'without disgust' for nirghṛṇa, to keep the source order (nighiṇa first) and a short line. Is that acceptable? The alternative is 'Kāṇha, kāpālika yogi, clings, past disgust'.
The source prints ধ্রু after couplet 1, before the refrain has been sung. Should the sung text print the refrain cue after couplet 1 as well, or only after couplets 3 to 7?

6a follows the accurate English's vocative ('You there, Ḍombī: I'm a kāpālika'). If you want to keep open its other reading ('you are a Ḍombī; I am a kāpālika'), a bare 'You, Ḍombī; I, kāpālika' would do it. The rhyme kapālī/mālī is lost either way. Could the sung line use the song's own form 'kapālī' instead of the approved 'kāpālika'?

7b drops the second 'I'll' ('I'll kill Ḍombī, take her life') so that it sings shorter and differs from the accurate line. If the paired first-person verbs (mārami, lemi) must both stay, the line becomes 'I'll kill Ḍombī, I'll take her life', which is almost the accurate English.
